omg.analysis.valid_atoms.ValidAtoms#

class omg.analysis.valid_atoms.ValidAtoms(atoms: Atoms, volume_check_cutoff: float = 0.1, structure_check_cutoff: float = 0.5, use_pauling_test: bool = True, include_alloys: bool = True, skip_validation: bool = False, upper_narity_limit: int | None = None)[source]#

Validate an Atoms object based on volume, structure, composition, and fingerprint checks.

This class is inspired by CDVAE’s/DiffCSP’s crystal class (see jiaor17/DiffCSP).

The volume is considered valid if it is bigger than a given cutoff (default: 0.1 Å^3).

The structure is considered valid if all pairwise distances are larger than a given cutoff (default: 0.5 Å).

The composition is considered valid if it is valid according to the SMACT rules. Because the checking of the SMACT rules can be slow for compositions with a high n-arity, the upper limit for the n-arity can be set. If the n-arity exceeds the upper limit, the composition is automatically considered invalid.

This class also computes the CrystalNN structural fingerprints and the normalized Magpie compositional fingerprints. If the computation of the fingerprints fails, the atoms are considered invalid.

Note that the (slow) composition and fingerprint checks are only run if the volume and structure checks pass.

Parameters:

  • atoms (Atoms) – The Atoms instance to validate.

  • volume_check_cutoff (float) – The cutoff for the volume check (in Å^3). Defaults to 0.1.

  • structure_check_cutoff (float) – The cutoff for the structure check (in angstroms). Defaults to 0.5.

  • use_pauling_test (bool) – Whether to use the Pauling test for the composition check. Defaults to True.

  • include_alloys (bool) – Whether to include alloys in the composition check. Defaults to True.

  • skip_validation (bool) – Whether to skip the validation and return a list of ValidAtoms instances with all properties set to True. Defaults to False.

  • upper_narity_limit (Optional[int]) – The upper limit for the n-arity of the composition. Compositions with a higher n-arity are automatically considered invalid in the SMACT check. If None, no limit is set. Defaults to None.
